name: Whiskey
description: A spirit distilled from fermented grain mash and aged in wooden casks. Made around the world in many styles, including bourbon, rye, Scotch, Irish, Canadian and Japanese.

name: American Whiskey
description: Whiskey made in the United States. Covers bourbon, rye, Tennessee, corn, wheat, single malt and blended styles, most of them aged in charred oak barrels.

name: Bourbon
description: American whiskey made from at least 51 percent corn and aged in new charred oak barrels. Sweet and full, with vanilla, caramel and oak. The base of the Old Fashioned, Whiskey Sour and Mint Julep.

name: Rye
description: Whiskey made from a mash of at least 51 percent rye in the American style, aged in new charred oak. Drier and spicier than bourbon. The classic base for the Manhattan and the Sazerac.

name: Bonded Rye
description: Rye whiskey bottled in bond: the product of one distillery and one season, aged at least four years and bottled at 100 proof. The extra strength holds up well in stirred drinks.

name: Tennessee Whiskey
description: Whiskey made in Tennessee to a bourbon-style recipe and filtered through sugar maple charcoal before ageing, a step known as the Lincoln County Process. Soft, sweet and lightly smoky.

name: Canadian Whisky
description: Whisky mashed, distilled and aged at least three years in Canada, usually a blend of light corn whisky and rye-heavy flavouring whisky. Often called rye in Canada. Light, smooth and gently spicy.

name: Corn Whiskey
description: Whiskey made from a mash of at least 80 percent corn. In the United States it is sold unaged or aged in used or uncharred barrels, which keeps it pale, sweet and grain forward.

name: American Single Malt Whiskey
description: Whiskey made at a single United States distillery from 100 percent malted barley. Styles vary by region and cask, from rich and malty to smoky.
